PROJECT

Demo Notes

Start with a project. The following actions stay connected to it.

First, know what to continue

With several projects and conversations open, “let it continue” is ambiguous. Control from a phone requires more than forwarding a command to a computer: the system needs to know its target. In CODY, I work on shared project and session context for voice and manual interaction. A user can express a short intention or select a conversation explicitly. When several targets are plausible, the interface offers a choice instead of acting on a guess.

The phone controls; the Mac holds state

The mobile app connects to a local Mac Bridge through a typed WebSocket protocol. The Bridge validates messages, maintains project and session information, and calls the relevant adapter. Terminal work persists in tmux independently of its visible window. Coding conversations use a session-provider integration layer. This boundary lets the phone stay compact: it presents state and available actions instead of trying to reproduce an entire desktop on a smaller screen.

A choice becomes a specific action

My implementation connects the mobile client and Bridge through a shared TypeScript/Zod protocol. Connections are authenticated and messages are checked at runtime. Available choices receive short-lived identifiers associated with the connection; the Bridge resolves them into specific operations. This separates the text on a button from the command itself. A more detailed workspace view provides conversation history and exact selection when a short voice exchange is not enough to choose the next step confidently.

A character that communicates state

CODY has a face and expressions for listening, thinking, working and encountering a problem. I connect that character to a practical interface task: helping the user understand what is happening. A short response supports quick interaction; a full history supports inspection. Both use the same context. Animation can make a state easier to notice, but it must not stand in for a result. A lost connection matters just as much as a successful completion.

The prototype’s boundaries

The mobile client, Bridge, shared protocol, context management and session adapters are implemented, with tests for messages, state, intent and Bridge behaviour. Voice interaction requires the app to be open and active; continuous background listening is not promised. This is a personal prototype with local setup, without a verified user-base or productivity claim. The sequence on this page illustrates a fictional task; it does not execute commands on the visitor’s device.

Conversational control becomes useful when a short phrase is backed by precise state and an action that can be checked.
